content: Paromomycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic that works by interfering with bacterial protein synthesis through binding to the 30S ribosomal subunits. It is effective against certain pathogenic organisms in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. This medication is poorly absorbed in the body and is excreted entirely in the feces as an unchanged drug. Paromomycin, commonly sold under the brand name Humatin, is primarily used to treat intestinal parasitic infections, such as amebiasis. It halts the growth of parasites in the intestines. Additionally, it may be prescribed alongside a special diet to manage hepatic encephalopathy, a serious brain condition caused by excessive ammonia levels in the body, often seen in individuals with liver disease. Normally, the liver removes ammonia from the body, but in liver disease, this process is impaired. This antibiotic is only effective against parasitic and bacterial infections and does not work for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. For optimal results, it should be taken at evenly spaced intervals. It is important to complete the full prescribed course of treatment, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects of paromomycin include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, abdominal cramps, diarrhea, and heartburn. While these side effects may occur, the medication is prescribed because the benefits are deemed greater than the risks. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or new vaginal yeast infections. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before taking paromomycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminoglycoside antibiotics (e.g., gentamicin, tobramycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Paromomycin may also reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, and it is unknown if it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how paromomycin works or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is essential to maintain a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as unconsciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) or a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can contact the poison control hotline at 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store paromomycin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into drains unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about paromomycin. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
